findings.title: DEC04 calendar/metric gap
findings.evidence: Current normal SLA is 9 working hours, Thursday+Friday excluded; urgent=4/high=8/low=27. Ticket has slaDueAt/resolvedAt/closedAt but no versioned calendar/target or first meaningful public response marker. Existing breach/summary is not the approved first-response metric.
findings.nextStep: Add an additive versioned policy/calendar snapshot and atomic eligible first-public-response event for new tickets only; separate resolution metric. Preserve old deadlines and unknown history. Do not change shared helper or data before scoped authorization/tests.

findings.title: Non-atomic claim/assignment
findings.evidence: Support can take an already assigned ticket for self; pre-read then id-only transactional update permits both concurrent claims and stale audit-before values.
findings.nextStep: Define authorized reassignment separately from claim; use expected-assignee/status CAS/locking and transaction-bound audit. Test two real DB connections and replay, without silently changing who may reassign.

findings.title: Terminal ticket and reopen drift
findings.evidence: reply/escalate/resolve lack terminal-state guards; public reply can reopen closed to waiting_customer, resolve can reopen closed and duplicate reports, while customer response on waiting_customer leaves status unchanged.
findings.nextStep: Explicit ticket transition and replay contract with non-destructive history; compare current UI and owner expectations, then scoped implementation and tests for all terminal/reopen paths.

findings.title: Blank text/reason accepted
findings.evidence: Ticket DTO string validators accept whitespace/empty strings; escalation persists reason but does not normalize or ensure meaningful nonblank value. This conflicts with the approved real server-side sensitive-reason rule.
findings.nextStep: Trim and bound text server-side; nonblank reason must be consumed in escalation/audit. Keep internal/public visibility and customer-confirmation no-fake-note contract. DTO/behavior fix needs scoped authority.

findings.title: Partial persistence and duplicate retry
findings.evidence: Reply/customer response/escalation use separate writes and Outbox may fail after message/status persists. Caller may see failure and resend, producing duplicates; notifyUser supports tx but reply does not supply it.
findings.nextStep: Atomic domain+Outbox transaction and payload-bound idempotency; preserve user text on retry; inject DB/Outbox/report failure and test rollback/concurrent replay.

findings.title: Unsupported support KPI
findings.evidence: supportPerformance counts every customer-visible message; aggregate without userId includes customer-authored messages, not only support replies. No meaningful-first-response denominator or period/provenance. It must not drive automated HR effects.
findings.nextStep: Role- and event-qualified metrics with interval, denominator and unknown state; separate first response/resolution and require human audited command for any sensitive staffing effect per DEC16.

findings.title: Repeated breach events
findings.evidence: flagOverdueTickets selects waiting_customer and has no first-response marker or breach-event deduplication; repeated calls append breach rows and urgent update for same still-overdue ticket, inflating KPI.
findings.nextStep: Versioned policy and one breach event per ticket/clock/policy generation; first-response clock must not pause while waiting_customer. Backfill neither historical first-response nor zero scores from unknown data.

findings.title: Admin command authority wider than DEC13 target
findings.evidence: Support controller declares support/admin RolesGuard only, no AdminScopeGuard. Current service skips assignee restriction for all admin roles; no Ops/Finance/Super per-command proxy capability. This is authenticated broad admin access, not anonymous access or proof of production exploit.
findings.nextStep: Implement explicit allowed command+subject capability and separate actor/owner audit in an independently authorized access package; preserve Support's zero financial authority and no impersonation.

authority: Documentation and isolated in-memory characterization only. DEC04/13/16 target approvals are not protected runtime/auth/DB exceptions. Fixed preservation baseline and the three existing invoice/pricing/reconciliation exceptions remain unchanged.
limits: Eight scoped write routes reviewed, not full Z0 or all remaining commands. AST/hash/DTO evidence is not authentication, SQL rollback, live notification, distributed concurrency, privacy export or E2E acceptance. GAP tests deliberately reproduce open behavior and must not be called fixes.
